syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Practical Work in Geography Part II

topics.title: What is data, need of data and its presentation
topics.ncert_sections: What is Data?; Need of Data; Presentation of the Data

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish data, a datum and information as defined in the chapter.
Explain why quantitative data are needed to study geographical phenomena such as cropping patterns and city growth.
Recognise how a statistical fallacy, such as relying on an average alone, can mislead conclusions.

topics.title: Sources of primary data
topics.ncert_sections: Sources of Data; Sources of Primary Data

concepts.learning_objective: Identify primary data and the methods used to collect it, including personal observation and field instruments.
State the precautions an interviewer should take while collecting information.
Distinguish between a questionnaire and a schedule and judge when each is suitable.

topics.title: Secondary sources of data
topics.ncert_sections: Secondary Source of Data; Published Sources; Unpublished Sources

concepts.learning_objective: Classify published secondary sources into government, quasi-government, international, private, newspaper and electronic sources.
Identify unpublished government, quasi-government and private records as secondary sources.

topics.title: Tabulation, compilation and presentation of data
topics.ncert_sections: Tabulation and Classification of Data; Data Compilation and Presentation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a statistical table and its purpose in summarising raw data.
Distinguish absolute data from percentage or ratio data and compute a rate such as literacy rate.
Calculate and interpret an index number by the simple aggregate method.

topics.title: Processing, grouping and frequency distribution
topics.ncert_sections: Processing of Data; Grouping of Data; Process of Classification; Frequency Distribution

concepts.learning_objective: Decide the number of classes and the class interval from the range of raw data.
Classify raw data into groups using the Four and Cross Method of tally marks.
Compute simple and cumulative frequencies and interpret them.

topics.title: Exclusive and inclusive methods of grouping

concepts.learning_objective: Place marginal values correctly into classes formed by the exclusive method.
Describe how classes are formed and values counted in the inclusive method.

topics.title: Frequency polygon and Ogive

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a frequency polygon and its use in comparing frequency distributions.
Construct and interpret less than and more than Ogives from cumulative frequencies.

topics.title: Statistical techniques and measures of central tendency

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish measures of central tendency, dispersion and relationship by what each one describes.
Explain why a measure of central tendency is a representative figure for a data set.

topics.title: Mean from ungrouped data: direct and indirect methods

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the mean of ungrouped data by the direct method.
Calculate the mean of ungrouped data by coding with an assumed mean.

topics.title: Mean from grouped data: direct and indirect methods

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the mean of a frequency distribution using class midpoints.
Calculate the mean of grouped data from deviations about an assumed mean group.

topics.title: Median for ungrouped and grouped data

concepts.learning_objective: Locate the median of an arranged series using the (N+1)/2 th item.
Compute the median of grouped data with cumulative frequencies and the median formula.

topics.title: Mode for ungrouped data

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the mode of an ungrouped series.
Classify a series as unimodal, bimodal, trimodal, multimodal or without mode.

topics.title: Comparison of mean, median and mode

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the normal curve and the coincidence of mean, median and mode in it.
Interpret the relative positions of mean, median and mode in skewed distributions.

topics.title: Representation of data and general rules for drawing graphs, diagrams and maps

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what representation of data means and why graphic methods aid understanding and comparison.
Select a suitable graphical method and scale for a given type of data.
Identify the title, legend and direction as components of cartographic design and their usual placement.

topics.title: Line graph and polygraph

concepts.learning_objective: Construct and interpret a line graph of time series data, including negative values.
Use a polygraph to compare two or more variables with distinct line patterns.

topics.title: Bar diagrams: simple, line and bar, multiple and compound

concepts.learning_objective: State the rules for constructing a simple bar diagram.
Combine a line graph and a bar diagram to show temperature and rainfall on one diagram.
Distinguish multiple and compound bar diagrams and choose the right one for given data.

topics.title: Pie diagram

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the angles of the sectors of a pie diagram from absolute or percentage data.
Describe the steps and precautions in constructing a pie diagram.

topics.title: Flow maps and charts

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the features of and requirements for a flow map.
Apply a scale to convert flow data into strips of proportional width.

topics.title: Thematic maps: dot maps and choropleth maps

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish quantitative and non-quantitative thematic maps.
State the requirements and precautions of a dot map and calculate the number of dots.
Group data into categories and prepare a choropleth map for administrative units.

topics.title: Isopleth maps and interpolation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify types of isopleths and the kind of data they represent.
Locate the exact point of an isopleth between two stations by interpolation.

topics.title: Spatial Information Technology and GIS
topics.ncert_sections: What is Spatial Information Technology?; What is GIS?; Forms of Geographical Information

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of spatial information and the technologies that make up Spatial Information Technology.
Define GIS and explain how it goes beyond database management and computer assisted cartography to support decisions.
Distinguish spatial data (positional, linear and areal) from non-spatial or attribute data.

topics.title: Sources of Spatial Data and Advantages of GIS
topics.ncert_sections: Forms of Geographical Information; Advantages of GIS over Manual Methods

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the ways spatial data are built in a GIS core and the factors governing the choice of a data source.
State the characteristics of topographical and thematic maps that make them a source of spatial data.
Evaluate the advantages of GIS over manual methods of map making and analysis.

topics.title: Components of GIS

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the five components of GIS and the role of each.
Relate GIS operations to the functional modules of GIS application software.

topics.title: Spatial Data Formats: Raster and Vector

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how raster data represent features as grid cells and how cell size affects resolution.
Describe how vector data represent features through coordinate pairs of points.
Compare the advantages, disadvantages and typical uses of raster and vector formats.

topics.title: Sequence of GIS Activities and Spatial Data Input
topics.ncert_sections: Sequence of GIS Activities; Spatial Data Input; Scanners

concepts.learning_objective: Arrange the activities involved in GIS-related work in their correct sequence.
Explain the compatibility checks needed when digital data sets from different suppliers are combined.
Explain how scanners convert analogue maps into digital raster images.

topics.title: Attribute Data, Verification, Editing and Conversion
topics.ncert_sections: Entering the Attribute Data; Data Verification and Editing; Data Conversion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify attribute data of spatial entities and the sources from which they are entered into GIS.
Identify common errors in captured spatial data and the methods used to verify and correct them.
Explain why and how data are converted between vector and raster formats.

topics.title: Geographic Data: Linkages and Matching

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why spatial and attribute data sets must be correctly linked in GIS.
Explain exact matching of files through a common key.
Distinguish hierarchical matching from fuzzy matching and choose the right one for a given data set.

topics.title: Spatial Analysis: Overlay and Buffer Operations
topics.ncert_sections: Spatial Analysis; Overlay Analysis Operations; Buffer Operation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain overlay analysis and its use in studying land use change and urban sprawl.
Apply buffer operations to proximity analysis of facilities and pollution sources.
